assessments.summary: Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 221% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, totaling 4,991 cases this year compared to 1,561 at the same time last year.
Dengue cases in the US are peaking with a 685% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, totaling 1,287 cases this year compared to 1,310 at the same time last year.
West Nile virus cases in the US are peaking with a 1,275% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, totaling 1,718 cases this year compared to 2,652 at the same time last year.
Influenza activity is rising with a 22% increase in global flu test positivity and a 76% rise in US hospital admissions compared to the previous month.
Mpox cases in the US are rising with a 72% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, totaling 1,500 cases this year compared to 2,128 at the same time last year.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US are rising with a 66% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, totaling 7,917 cases this year compared to 8,558 at the same time last year.
Hepatitis A cases in the US are at baseline with a 14% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, totaling 616 cases this year compared to 927 at the same time last year.
Malaria cases in the US are rising with a 52% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, totaling 1,147 cases this year compared to 1,424 at the same time last year.
RSV activity is rising globally and in the US, with test positivity increasing by 38% monthly and hospital admissions up 47% monthly.
Pertussis cases in the US are rising, with weekly reports up 50% over the past 8 months and annual cases exceeding last year's by 12,000.
US COVID-19 hospital admissions are slightly rising, with weekly numbers up 10% monthly, but activity remains at baseline.
Marburg virus disease activity is falling, with Wikipedia readership at the 57th percentile of the past year.
Chikungunya cases in the US are stable, with weekly reports down 1% over the past 8 months and annual cases slightly higher than last year.
Norovirus activity is stable, with Wikipedia readership at the 36th percentile of the past year.
Avian influenza (H5N1) activity is stable, with Wikipedia readership at the 38th percentile of the past year.
